clue.text: Why keep stale bread? It's of little value

definitions.meaning: first meaning: old bread is kept to be thrown out as food for garden birds
second meaning: the idiom for something worthless or trivial

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads literally (stale bread is kept to feed birds); the second is the idiom's figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'for the birds' means worthless, not worth bothering about, which matches something of little value.

clue.text: Sack employee, old member of train crew

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
a man can mean a worker, as in 'management and men'

explanation.surface: A railway worker of the past is dismissed from their job.
explanation.walkthrough: On a steam locomotive the fireman stoked the boiler, a job that vanished with steam, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireman was the stoker on a steam engine, part of the footplate crew alongside the driver.

clue.text: Final score left United going over amongst support

indicators.note: amongst says the flipped pair sits among the letters of the word for support

parts.note: a rest is a support, such as an armrest or a cue rest

indicators.note: going over signals that the pair of letters is flipped round, read in the opposite order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football report: the final score after a team called United is left over the support of fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns LU into UL, and 'amongst' places it inside REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the outcome of a match, the final score recorded at the whistle.

clue.text: Delay ambassador appearing on TV channel outside Italy

indicators.note: in a down clue, appearing on means placed on top of, so this piece comes first

parts.note: HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

indicators.note: outside says the channel word goes round the letter for Italy

parts.note: a station is a broadcasting channel
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An envoy's TV appearance is held up while they are away from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, the formal title of an ambassador. In a down entry, 'appearing on' means sitting on top, so that piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation is a pause before acting, a brief delay caused by uncertainty.

clue.text: Forest player on the bench, upset, attracting Hearts?

indicators.note: attracting means drawing another piece to its side, so the card letter is added on
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a sub (substitute) waits on the bench
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A Nottingham Forest substitute, sulking on the bench, catches the eye of Hearts, the Edinburgh football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forest' looks like the football club Nottingham Forest, but it is the definition; 'upset' turns SUB into BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush is wild uncultivated country covered with scrub or woodland, as in the Australian bush.

clue.text: Style differently flag British vessel flies, removing name

indicators.note: removing says that letter is taken out of the flag's name

parts.note: the Red Ensign is the flag flown by British merchant ships

explanation.surface: Restyling the flag a British ship flies, minus its name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Ensign, the 'Red Duster', is the flag of the British merchant navy; dropping one N leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To redesign is to give something a new design, changing how it is styled.

clue.text: Hide from view regularly car seat's splits

indicators.note: splits says these letters break the word for view apart, sitting inside it

parts.note: to view is to see

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, at a regular interval

explanation.surface: Someone hides a car seat whose upholstery has split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide from view' looks like the whole definition, but 'view' belongs to the wordplay and 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete something is to conceal it or stash it away out of sight.

clue.text: Checks parts of chair moggy originally scratched

indicators.note: scratched means struck out, so that letter is deleted

parts.note: armrests are parts of an armchair

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: first letter of moggy; a moggy is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat has clawed the arms of a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Moggy is British slang for an ordinary cat, which fits 'scratched' in the surface; here it supplies M to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrests is a verb form meaning halts or stops, the same as checks progress.

clue.text: Numbers turning up taking part in several discos?

parts.note: to be at an event is to be present, taking part in it
ten is used loosely as one of several numbers
discos are dances

explanation.surface: How many people come along when someone goes to several discos.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the loose wordplay: 'at ten dances' describes taking part in several discos.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendances are counts of people who come to events, the numbers present on each occasion.

clue.text: Retired soccer ace disinclined to accept cocktail

indicators.note: Retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
to accept says the words hold the answer inside them, accepting it within

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A retired football star is reluctant to accept a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'to accept cocktail' as the definition, but 'to accept' is the containment signal: the words accept RACEDIS, which 'Retired' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a classic mixed drink of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Nostalgic of late describing archetypal 1960s cars

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round, as a circle is described, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: something of late is recent
the Mini was the iconic small British car of the sixties

explanation.surface: A nostalgic recent piece describing the classic cars of the sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in the geometric sense of drawing a line round something, as you describe a circle, so it signals one piece enclosing another.
explanation.definitionFit: Reminiscent means evoking memories of the past, which is what nostalgic feeling does.

clue.text: Model, one on short-term contract possibly, departed

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker, often on a short contract
the late person is one who has died, departed this life

explanation.surface: A fashion model on a short-term deal has walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or exemplar from which copies are made, so a model.

clue.text: Comes across European about to get honour

indicators.note: about signals turning the combined letters round to run the other way

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: A European comes across someone about to receive an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'about to get', but it reverses MEETS + E.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in high regard, to honour or respect them.

clue.text: Ahead of Cup winger shows class

indicators.note: Ahead of says the bird comes before the golf term

parts.note: a winger is something with wings, here a bird such as a pigeon
in golf the hole is also called the cup

explanation.surface: A football winger shows real class in the run-up to a cup tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winger' suggests a footballer, but it is a bird; 'class' is a verb, to categorise.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole something is to assign it to a category, to classify it.

clue.text: Visiting Northumberland area, working for nothing

indicators.note: Visiting means going into a place, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: NE, the north-east of England, where Northumberland is
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone visiting Northumberland works for no pay.
explanation.definitionFit: None means not any, so it can stand for nothing at all.

clue.text: Vegetable banger isn't cooked!

indicators.note: cooked suggests letters prepared into a new form, rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation that this sausage isn't cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage, which suits 'cooked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A string bean is a green bean, a vegetable eaten pod and all.

clue.text: Sign of maybe permanently closed restaurant for celebrities

definitions.text: Sign of maybe permanently closed restaurant
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a notice saying the place has ..., perhaps because it has shut

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the answer as 'no tables', a sign either of a full or of a shut restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Notables are people of distinction or fame, which is what celebrities are.

clue.text: One predicting exciting future perhaps, right after great solo plays

indicators.note: after says this letter follows the rearranged letters
plays suggests letters moving about freely, so these are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A soloist plays brilliantly, which may foretell an exciting future.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer forecasts what lies ahead from the stars, perhaps promising good things.

clue.text: Got on with extremely top-notch diver at sea

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outermost letters of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of top-notch

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A first-class diver who got on well in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to do well or prosper, so thrived means got on, made progress.

clue.text: Contends movie star is inspiring

indicators.note: is inspiring says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A film star competes and inspires others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' is used literally as breathing in, so the words take the answer inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete, so vies means contends or struggles for something.

clue.text: This writer's indeed including German figures of speech

parts.note: the setter speaking: this writer is = I'm

indicators.note: including says the word for indeed holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect yes, indeed

explanation.surface: A writer says they really do include German expressions.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'This writer's' is 'is', so the setter is saying I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is the collective term for metaphors and other vivid figurative language.

clue.text: Almost fail to get strong fish out of water

indicators.note: Almost says the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit
fit means healthy and strong

explanation.surface: A strong fish nearly fails to survive out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish out of water' reads literally in the surface, but it is the idiom for someone who does not belong.
explanation.definitionFit: A misfit is a person who does not fit in, like someone uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.

clue.text: Popular breakfast TV programme broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out over the air, so the word heard is a different one spelt otherwise

parts.note: a serial is a TV drama shown in episodes

explanation.surface: A popular breakfast television programme goes out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal, such as cornflakes, is the commonest morning meal in a bowl.

clue.text: Friend of bully I'd avoided

indicators.note: avoided says those letters are kept out, removed from the longer word

parts.note: to bully is to intimidate
I'd without its apostrophe gives these two letters

explanation.surface: Someone avoided a friend of a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate is a close confidant, a very familiar companion.

clue.text: Key error admitted by party-pooper

indicators.note: admitted by says the answer is let in, held inside the following word

parts.note: the letters run across the hyphen from one part into the next

explanation.surface: A killjoy confesses to a crucial mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key error' looks like a crucial mistake, but means a slip on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a typing mistake, hitting the wrong key.

clue.text: Sausage made from veal, liberally dipped in sauce

indicators.note: dipped in says the rearranged letters go inside the sauce

parts.note: soy is a sauce

indicators.note: liberally means freely, so the letters are moved about freely

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A sausage of veal generously dunked in sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: A saveloy is a seasoned red sausage sold in British chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A saveloy is a highly seasoned smoked pork sausage, a British chip-shop staple.

clue.text: Not keeping time musically? That's unusual

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as off the beat: out of time with the music

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as 'off beat'; strictly the offbeat is the unstressed beat, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Offbeat describes something unconventional or eccentric, which is to say unusual.

clue.text: Attractive sort, just acquiring oddly vacant bedsit using deceit

parts.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person

indicators.note: acquiring says the word for just takes the letters inside it

parts.note: just means only

indicators.note: oddly vacant says the odd-placed letters are emptied out, leaving the even ones

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of bedsit

explanation.surface: A good-looking person just takes over an empty bedsit by trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit is a British one-room flat. 'oddly vacant' empties it of B, D, I, leaving EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonestly means in a lying or fraudulent way, by deceit.
